clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Thursday, April 15, 1915, the only day on which it closes the executive offices and directs the half-mast display and tribute ('on Thursday, April 15, 1915, the fiftieth anniversary of his death'). The dossier holds no own-terms record for this order, so the end cites the order's complete held text, which contains the stated day.

research_rationale:
EO 2171 (April 13, 1915, Woodrow Wilson), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan text (jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_2171.txt; grade archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held) and checked against the page image I rendered on 2026-10-28 from the held PDF ('ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1915-EO-2171.pdf', sha256 6887d229..., equal to the registry's; one page; heading 'Executive Order', signature 'WOODROW WILSON', date '13 April, 1915', printed '[No. 2171.]', handwritten '2171' at top). The OCR layer is complete; its first line (']Executive 1t'rer') is the misread heading 'Executive Order', not order text. The order directs that the executive offices of the United States be closed, that the national flag be displayed at half-mast on all Federal buildings, forts, military posts, naval stations and vessels of the United States, and that the representatives of the United States in foreign countries pay tribute in like manner, 'on Thursday, April 15, 1915, the fiftieth anniversary of his death' (Abraham Lincoln's). Its second paragraph only requests owners and masters of merchant ships to display the flag at half-mast; a request is not a command. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the scan, the registry record (signing date 1915-04-13) and the census register. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1915-04-15, the only day it governs; a reader who dates cessation to the first day without effect would write 1915-04-16, and this claim records 1915-04-15, the day through whose end the order ran, consistent with the owner's inclusive reading of stated dates. Searches made on 2026-10-28: census register titles and the WPA 1944 numbered list for 1915 Lincoln or half-mast orders, and a citation search of every held order text for 'No. 2171' and 'Order No. 2171'. The only citation hit, in jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_7870.txt, amends an 'Administrative Order No. 2171', a different instrument. Nothing names EO 2171. The machine USC and eCFR searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone.
